$comment: Prompt library. Demo data from Nexus design reference; every record is a sample (source_kind). Desks decide whose prompts show first: a person is on the desk whose job_titles holds their directory job title.

risk_levels.Low: Operates on documents already held inside the MUFG boundary. No external transmission.
risk_levels.Medium: Handles client or portfolio data. Mask identifiers before upload — the prompt stops if it detects an unmasked account number.
risk_levels.High: Deal-sensitive or control-facing. Restricted to a cleared team; every run is logged and reviewable by Compliance.

templates.name: Analysis and synthesis
templates.use: Turn a document into a structured written narrative
templates.when: Credit memos, MD&A sections, research summaries
templates.body:
ROLE: You are a {{SENIORITY}} {{FUNCTION}} at MUFG.

INPUT: {{ATTACHED DOCUMENT}}

TASK
{{WHAT TO ANALYSE}}. Write a {{LENGTH}}-word {{OUTPUT TYPE}} explaining
{{THE QUESTION THE READER NEEDS ANSWERED}}.

MUST COVER
- {{POINT 1}}
- {{POINT 2}}
- {{POINT 3}}

CONSTRAINTS
- Reference only figures present in the attachment; never estimate.
- State the definition used for any ratio or metric.
- Flag anything unverifiable as [VERIFY] rather than filling the gap.
- Do not state a recommendation or a decision.

templates.name: Extraction and flagging
templates.use: Pull specific clauses, signals or exceptions out of long documents
templates.when: Covenant scans, regulatory gap analysis, transcript mining
templates.body:
ROLE: You are a {{FUNCTION}} analyst at MUFG.

INPUT: {{SOURCE DOCUMENT}}
LOOKING FOR: {{WHAT TO FIND}}

TASK
Extract every instance of {{TARGET ITEM}} and rank by {{RANKING BASIS}}.

RETURN A TABLE
| Item | Source reference | Trigger or condition | Consequence
| Materiality | Action owner | Needs human review? |

CONSTRAINTS
- Cite the paragraph or clause reference for every item.
- Never characterise an item as immaterial without its reference.
- Where the source is ambiguous, mark AMBIGUOUS — do not interpret.

templates.name: Scenario and stress
templates.use: Apply a shock to a model or portfolio and describe the impact
templates.when: DSCR stress tests, rate shocks, concentration analysis
templates.body:
ROLE: You are a {{FUNCTION}} analyst at MUFG.

BASE CASE: {{MODEL OR PORTFOLIO DATA}}
SHOCK: {{SCENARIO PARAMETERS}}

TASK
Simulate {{SCENARIO}} and describe the impact on {{KEY METRIC}}.

RETURN
1. {{KEY METRIC}} base vs stressed, and when the minimum occurs
2. First breach or limit date, with headroom at each test point
3. Two mitigants available, ranked by effectiveness
4. A {{LENGTH}}-word paragraph in {{COMMITTEE}} register

CONSTRAINTS
- State every convention and model version used.
- Mark any assumption not sourced from the input as ANALYST INPUT.
- Indicative only — rerun in the sanctioned model before any decision.

templates.name: Client-facing draft
templates.use: Produce a narrative or email a client will eventually read
templates.when: Pitch outlines, advisory emails, RFP responses
templates.body:
ROLE: You are a {{FUNCTION}} at MUFG covering {{CLIENT NAME}}.

CONTEXT
- Client situation: {{SITUATION}}
- What we are proposing: {{MUFG SOLUTION}}
- The client's stated goal: {{CLIENT GOAL}}

TASK
Draft {{DELIVERABLE}} in {{LENGTH}} words, consultative in tone,
with one clear next step.

FOR EACH POINT
- The benefit to the client, led by a number from the attachment
- The MUFG capability that delivers it
- The objection it pre-empts

CONSTRAINTS
- No marketing superlatives; senior and precise.
- Never state pricing that has not been confirmed by Product.
- Internal draft until reviewed — mark it as such in the footer.

prompts.title: Corporate pitch structurer
prompts.description: Turns a client financial history and industry outlook into a five-point pitch deck outline for a revolving credit facility RFP.
prompts.repetition: Replaces 4 manual deck drafts per RFP
prompts.narrative: Cuts RFP turnaround from three days to half a day, so coverage teams respond first.
prompts.risk_note: No client identifiers leave the MUFG private model boundary. Attachments are stripped of account numbers before processing.

tutorial.title: Structuring an RFP response in 8 minutes

inputs.label: Client financial history
inputs.note: 3-year P&L and balance sheet (PDF or XLSX)

guidelines: Use only client documents already filed in the deal room — never paste material non-public information from a call.
The outline is a starting draft. Pricing and covenant language must be confirmed with Product and Credit before it reaches the client.
Attach the MUFG Research sector note rather than a third-party report, for licensing reasons.
Log the generated deck in the CRM against the deal ID so Credit can see the pitched structure.
prompts.body:
ROLE: You are a senior corporate banking coverage analyst at MUFG.

CONTEXT
- Client: {{CLIENT NAME}}
- Facility requested: {{FACILITY SIZE AND TENOR}}
- Client's stated 3-year goal: {{EXPANSION GOAL}}
- Attached: 3-year financial history, MUFG sector outlook

TASK
Analyse the attached client financial history, the current industry
macroeconomic trends, and MUFG's standard corporate lending parameters.
Generate a polished 5-point pitch deck outline explaining why our capital
structuring fits the client's 3-year expansion goal.

FOR EACH OF THE 5 POINTS RETURN
1. Slide headline (max 9 words, benefit-led)
2. Three supporting bullets, each anchored to a number from the financials
3. The MUFG capability that delivers it
4. The client objection this slide pre-empts

CONSTRAINTS
- Reference only figures present in the attachments; never estimate.
- Flag any metric where the source year is ambiguous as [VERIFY].
- Tone: precise, senior, no marketing superlatives.
prompts.sample_output:
5-POINT PITCH OUTLINE — Revolving Credit Facility

1. "Funding that flexes with your build cycle"
   • Capex ramp of USD 310m in FY25 vs USD 190m FY24 (+63%)
   • Peak working capital gap of ~USD 120m in Q3 each year
   • Current facility fully drawn 7 of the last 8 quarters
   → MUFG capability: multi-currency revolver with accordion
   → Pre-empts: "we don't want to hold idle committed capital"

2. "Leverage headroom preserved through the expansion"
   • Net debt/EBITDA at 2.4x vs 3.5x covenant ceiling
   • EBITDA margin expansion of 180bps YoY [VERIFY FY24 basis]
   ...

reviews.name: Henry Tucker
reviews.comment: Used this for a JPY 40bn RFP last week. The objection-handling line under each slide is what makes it different — the client raised exactly the concern it flagged and I already had the answer.

reviews.name: Paige Norton
reviews.comment: Excellent structure. One caution: it can over-index on the most recent year if your attachment has a stub period. I now trim the file before uploading.

reviews.name: James Whitfield
reviews.comment: Saved a full weekend on a competitive refinancing. Pair it with the Capital markets opportunity finder for the cross-sell page.

prompts.title: Capital markets opportunity finder
prompts.description: Reads an earnings call transcript for debt maturities, buybacks and capex signals, then maps them to MUFG bond underwriting capabilities.
prompts.repetition: Removes a 90-minute manual transcript read per client
prompts.narrative: Proactively flags multi-million dollar underwriting opportunities before the CFO meeting.
prompts.risk_note: Operates only on publicly disclosed transcripts. The prompt refuses to process documents marked internal or draft.

tutorial.title: Reading an earnings call like a DCM banker

guidelines: Public transcripts only. Never upload a draft transcript or a recording of a private management meeting.
Recommendations are hypotheses for discussion, not committed pricing. Route to DCM for indicative levels.
If the client is on the restricted list, stop — the prompt will warn you but you own the check.
Record any opportunity you pursue in the pipeline tool within 48 hours.
prompts.body:
ROLE: You are a debt capital markets origination analyst at MUFG.

INPUT: {{EARNINGS TRANSCRIPT}} for {{CLIENT NAME}} ({{TICKER}})

TASK
Review this quarterly earnings call transcript. Identify any mentions of:
  a) upcoming debt maturities or refinancing intentions
  b) share buyback programmes
  c) capital expenditure plans or M&A ambitions
  d) credit rating commentary or leverage targets

Cross-reference each signal with MUFG's bond underwriting capabilities
and output 3 specific corporate bond issuance recommendations.

OUTPUT FORMAT — for each recommendation
| Signal quoted | Speaker & timestamp | Implied need | Proposed MUFG solution
| Indicative size | Why now | Question to ask the CFO |

RULES
- Quote the transcript verbatim for each signal, max one sentence.
- If a signal is inferred rather than stated, label it INFERRED.
- Do not estimate pricing or spreads.
prompts.sample_output:
3 ISSUANCE RECOMMENDATIONS

1. Signal: "our 2027 notes come due in the back half of next year"
   Speaker: CFO, Q&A 41:20 | Implied need: refinancing window
   Proposed: USD senior unsecured, 5yr benchmark, pre-funded Q1
   Question to ask: "Are you targeting the pre-Golden Week window?"

2. Signal: capex guidance raised to USD 1.2bn (INFERRED funding gap)
   ...

reviews.name: Rachel Donovan
reviews.comment: This is the one I run before every CFO meeting. The "question to ask" column turns an analysis into an actual conversation opener.

reviews.name: Christopher Wade
reviews.comment: The INFERRED labelling matters. It stops you from telling a CFO they said something they did not say.

prompts.title: FX and cash management summary
prompts.description: Spots idle balances across multi-currency accounts and drafts a liquidity advisory email recommending cash pooling.
prompts.repetition: Replaces manual review of 20+ account statements
prompts.narrative: Turns dormant balances into a fee conversation the same afternoon.
prompts.risk_note: Handles account balance data. Account numbers must be masked before upload — the prompt rejects files where an unmasked IBAN pattern is detected.

tutorial.title: Building a liquidity advisory in one pass

inputs.label: Client treasury policy
inputs.note: If available — sets minimum balance rules

guidelines: Mask all account numbers to the last four digits before uploading. The prompt will stop if it finds a full IBAN.
Check the client treasury policy for minimum operating balances before calling a balance "idle".
The draft email is internal until Product signs off on the pooling structure and the local regulatory position.
Cross-border pooling is restricted in several APAC jurisdictions — confirm with local Treasury Product.
prompts.body:
ROLE: You are a transaction banking liquidity advisor at MUFG.

INPUT: {{ACCOUNT STATEMENTS}} covering {{TARGET CURRENCIES}}
Optional: {{CLIENT TREASURY POLICY}}

TASK
Based on the attached multi-currency account statements, identify patterns
where cash balances are sitting idle in low-interest accounts.

ANALYSIS STEPS
1. Compute average, minimum and peak balance per account per month.
2. Flag any account holding above its operating minimum for 15+ consecutive days.
3. Quantify the annualised opportunity cost at current rates by currency.
4. Identify the trapped-cash jurisdictions that pooling cannot solve.

THEN
Draft an advisory email to the client's Group Treasurer recommending
MUFG automated cash-pooling and liquidity management services.
Tone: consultative, 200 words max, one clear next step.

CONSTRAINTS
- Never state a rate we have not published internally.
- Mark restricted-currency accounts as "structurally trapped", not "idle".
prompts.sample_output:
IDLE BALANCE FINDINGS

• THB account (…4821): avg THB 240m held 26 days/month above operating min
• SGD account (…9903): peaks after quarterly collections, undeployed 18 days
• KRW: structurally trapped — pooling not permitted, recommend local sweep

Estimated annualised opportunity cost: USD 1.9m equivalent

DRAFT EMAIL — "A closer look at your APAC balances"
Dear ...

reviews.name: Travis Fletcher
reviews.comment: The "structurally trapped" distinction saved me from making a recommendation that would have been illegal in one market. Good guardrail.

reviews.name: Leah Harper
reviews.comment: Works well. The email draft is a little formal for long-standing clients — I rewrite the opening line every time.

prompts.title: KYC onboarding pre-screener
prompts.description: Builds the ownership tree and flags missing KYC documentation before the file reaches the onboarding team.
prompts.repetition: Prevents an average of 2 rejection cycles per file
prompts.narrative: Files reach onboarding complete the first time, cutting days off account opening.
prompts.risk_note: Processes beneficial ownership data. Output is confidential and must stay inside the onboarding case file.

tutorial.title: A clean KYC file, first time

guidelines: This is a pre-screen, not a KYC decision. Financial Crime Compliance owns the outcome.
Do not upload passport scans or personal identity documents into the prompt.
Escalate any ownership chain that passes through a high-risk jurisdiction directly to FCC.
Delete the working output once the case file is created.
prompts.body:
ROLE: You are a client onboarding analyst at MUFG.

INPUT: {{REGISTRY EXTRACT}} for entity operating in {{JURISDICTIONS}}

TASK
1. Build the ultimate beneficial ownership tree to the 10% threshold.
2. Compare the documents present against the MUFG KYC checklist
   for each jurisdiction listed.
3. Output a gap list ranked by what will block account opening first.

OUTPUT
- Ownership tree (indented, with % held at each level)
- Missing document table: document | entity | jurisdiction | blocking? 
- Three questions to ask the client in one consolidated email

CONSTRAINTS
- Never infer ownership percentages that are not documented.
- Mark any chain reaching a high-risk jurisdiction as ESCALATE TO FCC.
- Do not process personal identity documents.
prompts.sample_output:
UBO TREE (10% threshold)
Holdco Ltd (Singapore)
 ├── 62% — Regional Investments Pte
 │    └── 100% — Founder family trust ⚠ ESCALATE TO FCC (Cayman)
 └── 21% — Institutional fund (listed, exempt)

MISSING DOCUMENTS — 4 blocking, 2 non-blocking ...

reviews.name: Grace Alden
reviews.comment: The blocking/non-blocking split is the useful part. It tells the RM what to chase today versus what can follow.

prompts.title: Financial narrative builder
prompts.description: Converts a three-year comparative balance sheet into the Management Discussion and Analysis section of a credit memo.
prompts.repetition: Removes the blank-page problem on every credit application
prompts.narrative: Analysts start editing instead of drafting — memo cycle time down by a third.
prompts.risk_note: Works on borrower financials already inside the credit file. No external transmission; output is drafted into the memo template.

tutorial.title: From spreadsheet to MD&A in one prompt

inputs.label: 3-year comparative financials
inputs.note: Balance sheet and income statement, XLSX

guidelines: Always attach the auditor notes. Without them the model will read one-off gains as operating performance.
Every ratio in the output must be re-checked against the spreading tool before the memo is submitted.
The narrative explains drivers; it must not state a credit recommendation. That is your judgement.
If the borrower has changed accounting standards mid-period, say so explicitly in the memo.
prompts.body:
ROLE: You are a senior credit analyst at MUFG writing a credit application.

INPUT: {{3-YEAR FINANCIALS}}
Optional: {{AUDITOR NOTES}}

TASK
Review the attached 3-year comparative balance sheet and income statement.
Calculate the year-on-year changes in EBITDA margin and leverage ratio.
Write a dense, professional {{WORD COUNT}}-word executive summary explaining
the primary drivers behind the margin contraction or expansion.

MUST COVER
- Revenue quality: organic vs acquired, one-offs stripped out
- EBITDA margin bridge: price, volume, mix, cost inflation
- Leverage: gross and net debt/EBITDA, with the definition used
- Working capital swing and its cash impact
- Two drivers to monitor into the next reporting period

CONSTRAINTS
- State the definition used for every ratio.
- Separate reported from adjusted figures at all times.
- Do not state a credit recommendation or a rating.
- Flag any restatement or accounting standard change explicitly.
prompts.sample_output:
MANAGEMENT DISCUSSION & ANALYSIS (draft, 300 words)

EBITDA margin contracted 180bps to 21.4% (FY26: reported, IFRS 16 basis)
from 23.2% in FY25. The contraction is driven principally by input cost
inflation of ~240bps, partially offset by 60bps of price realisation...

Leverage: net debt/EBITDA 2.4x (net debt excludes lease liabilities;
including leases, 3.1x). Gross debt rose USD 180m on the September
issuance...

⚠ FY25 restated for the disposal of the logistics segment.

reviews.name: Sarah Kendall
reviews.comment: The insistence on stating the ratio definition has caught two disagreements between me and the RM before they reached committee. Worth the extra lines.

reviews.name: Martin Ashford
reviews.comment: Best prompt in the library. It refuses to give you a recommendation, which is exactly right — that is our job, not the model.

reviews.name: Julia Nolan
reviews.comment: Very strong on manufacturing names. For financial institutions borrowers the margin bridge does not really apply — a sector variant would help.

prompts.title: Project finance downside stress tester
prompts.description: Simulates tariff and delay shocks against a base-case model and drafts the DSCR impact section of the credit memo.
prompts.repetition: Replaces 6 manual scenario runs
prompts.narrative: Downside cases that used to take a day are ready before the credit committee papers close.
prompts.risk_note: Model outputs are indicative. The prompt must not be used as the sole basis for a covenant decision — rerun in the sanctioned financial model.
guidelines: Use the sanctioned base-case model only. Analyst working copies produce numbers that will not reconcile at committee.
Rerun any scenario that changes the sanctioning decision in the official model before it goes into the memo.
State the DSCR calculation convention — pre or post debt service reserve account.
Include the construction delay liquidated damages offset; the model does not assume it automatically.
prompts.body:
ROLE: You are a structured finance credit analyst at MUFG.

INPUT: {{BASE CASE MODEL}} and {{DEBT TERMS SHEET}}
STRESS: {{STRESS PARAMETERS}}

TASK
Given the base-case financial model attached, simulate a scenario where
{{STRESS PARAMETERS}} apply. Draft the credit memo section outlining the
impact on the project's minimum DSCR and its ability to service senior debt.

RETURN
1. Minimum DSCR and the period in which it occurs, base vs stressed
2. Average DSCR and loan life coverage ratio across the tenor
3. First covenant breach date, if any, and headroom at each test date
4. Cash available for debt service bridge, base vs stressed
5. Two mitigants available to the lender group, ranked by effectiveness
6. A 150-word memo paragraph in MUFG credit committee register

CONSTRAINTS
- State the DSCR convention used (pre/post DSRA).
- Apply liquidated damages offset for construction delay if in the terms.
- Mark any assumption not sourced from the attachments as ANALYST INPUT.
prompts.sample_output:
STRESSED CASE — tariff −15%, COD delay 6 months

Minimum DSCR   1.08x (base 1.34x) — occurs Q3 2029, post-DSRA basis
Average DSCR   1.21x (base 1.46x)
LLCR           1.19x (base 1.41x)
First breach   Q3 2029, 1.10x covenant — headroom −0.02x

LD offset applied: 4 months of delay covered by contractor LDs
Residual exposure: 2 months of unfunded interest ...

reviews.name: Michael Barrett
reviews.comment: The forced statement of the DSCR convention ended a recurring argument in our team. Two people were computing pre-DSRA and two post-DSRA.

reviews.name: Peter Lawson
reviews.comment: Solid for renewables. For toll roads I still hand-build the traffic ramp scenarios.

prompts.title: Bridge loan refinancing risk scanner
prompts.description: Flags restrictive covenants, change-of-control clauses and maturity walls in a target company debt profile ahead of an M&A bridge.
prompts.repetition: Replaces a full manual read of 8+ facility agreements
prompts.narrative: Surfaces the change-of-control landmines before the bank commits to the bridge.
prompts.risk_note: Deal-sensitive. Use only inside a cleared deal team with the information barrier in place. Every run is logged and reviewable by Compliance.
guidelines: Confirm you are wall-crossed on this deal before running. The prompt records your ID against the deal reference.
Never share the output outside the cleared deal team, including with coverage colleagues.
Clause extraction is a first pass. Legal must confirm every change-of-control trigger before commitment.
Delete local copies once the commitment paper is filed.
prompts.body:
ROLE: You are a leveraged finance analyst at MUFG. Deal ID {{DEAL ID}}.

INPUT: {{TARGET DEBT DOCUMENTATION}}
PROPOSED: {{BRIDGE STRUCTURE}}

TASK
Analyse the target company's debt profile. Flag all restrictive covenants,
change-of-control clauses and upcoming maturity walls that could impact
MUFG's refinancing risk if the M&A deal closes.

RETURN A RANKED RISK TABLE
| Instrument | Clause type | Trigger | Consequence on close
| Quantum at risk | Cure or waiver route | Legal review needed? |

THEN
- A maturity wall chart by year for the next 5 years
- The three clauses most likely to require a consent solicitation
- Estimated consent timeline and its effect on the bridge takeout

CONSTRAINTS
- Quote the operative clause reference for every flag.
- Never characterise a clause as benign without the reference.
- Mark anything requiring legal interpretation as LEGAL REVIEW.
prompts.sample_output:
RANKED REFINANCING RISKS — 11 flags, 4 critical

1. 2029 Senior Notes, cl. 4.14 — change of control put at 101
   Quantum at risk: USD 750m | Consent route: solicitation, ~6 weeks
   LEGAL REVIEW — "Permitted Holder" definition may exclude the acquirer

2. Revolving facility, cl. 22.3 — mandatory prepayment on CoC
   ...

MATURITY WALL: USD 1.9bn falls due in 2029 (68% of total debt)

reviews.name: Rebecca Stone
reviews.comment: The requirement to quote a clause reference for every flag is what makes this usable in a commitment paper. No unsourced assertions.

prompts.title: Covenant compliance monitor
prompts.description: Checks a borrower compliance certificate against the facility agreement and drafts the exception note for the watchlist.
prompts.repetition: Automates a quarterly check across the whole borrower book
prompts.narrative: Breaches are caught in the reporting week, not at the next annual review.
prompts.risk_note: Operates on documents already held in the credit file. Output routes to the watchlist workflow.

tutorial.title: Quarterly covenant checks without the spreadsheet

guidelines: The facility agreement definition always wins over the borrower calculation. Check both.
A near-miss inside 10% headroom must be raised even where there is no breach.
Do not close the monitoring task on the model output alone — a human sign-off is required.
prompts.body:
ROLE: You are a credit portfolio monitoring analyst at MUFG.

INPUT: {{COMPLIANCE CERTIFICATE}} and {{FACILITY AGREEMENT}}

TASK
Recalculate each financial covenant using the definitions in the facility
agreement, not the borrower's stated method. Compare against the certificate.

RETURN
| Covenant | Required | Borrower stated | Recalculated | Headroom % | Status |
Status is one of: COMPLIANT / NEAR MISS (<10% headroom) / BREACH / UNVERIFIABLE

THEN draft a 120-word exception note for the watchlist committee covering
what moved, whether it is structural or one-off, and the next test date.

CONSTRAINTS
- Show the definition text you applied for any covenant where you differ
  from the borrower's calculation.
- Mark UNVERIFIABLE rather than estimating a missing input.
prompts.sample_output:
COVENANT CHECK — Q2 2026

Net leverage    ≤3.50x  | stated 3.28x | recalc 3.41x | 2.6% | NEAR MISS
  Difference: borrower nets lease liabilities; cl. 1.1 does not permit this
Interest cover  ≥3.00x  | stated 4.10x | recalc 4.10x | 36%  | COMPLIANT
Capex limit     ≤USD 200m | stated 188m | UNVERIFIABLE — schedule missing

reviews.name: Paige Norton
reviews.comment: Caught a lease-netting difference on a borrower we had rated compliant for two quarters. That alone justified the rollout.

prompts.title: Concentration sensitivity analyst
prompts.description: Maps how an interest rate shock moves default probabilities across a sector-concentrated lending portfolio.
prompts.repetition: Replaces a week of manual sector slicing
prompts.narrative: Gives the risk committee a defensible concentration view the same week the rates move.
prompts.risk_note: Portfolio-level data only, aggregated above the single-borrower threshold. Never upload obligor-level exposures with names attached.

inputs.label: Portfolio exposure data
inputs.note: Aggregated by sector and rating band, CSV

guidelines: Aggregate above the single-borrower threshold before upload. Obligor names must not appear in the file.
Results are indicative and do not replace the sanctioned stress-testing platform for regulatory submissions.
State the PD model version used; committee papers are rejected without it.
Any output that changes the sector appetite recommendation goes through the Head of Portfolio Risk.
prompts.body:
ROLE: You are a portfolio risk analyst at MUFG.

INPUT: {{PORTFOLIO EXPOSURE DATA}}, {{PD TERM STRUCTURE}}
SHOCK: {{SHOCK DEFINITION}}

TASK
Analyse the attached bank-wide industrial lending portfolio data. Run a
thematic analysis mapping how a {{SHOCK DEFINITION}} would specifically
impact the default probabilities of our highly leveraged borrowers
in the {{SECTOR}} sector.

RETURN
1. Exposure by sector and rating band, pre and post shock
2. PD migration matrix — which bands move, and by how much
3. Expected loss delta in USD and in basis points of the book
4. The three sub-sectors carrying the most convexity
5. Concentration limit headroom after the shock
6. A 200-word summary for the Risk Committee pack

CONSTRAINTS
- State the PD model version and the as-of date.
- Do not name individual obligors.
- Distinguish contractual exposure from drawn exposure throughout.
prompts.sample_output:
+200BPS PARALLEL SHIFT — RETAIL SECTOR

Exposure       USD 14.2bn drawn / USD 21.8bn contractual
PD migration   BB band +140bps, B band +410bps (PD model v7.3, 30 Jun 26)
EL delta       +USD 186m (+13bps of the book)

Most convex sub-sectors
 1. Specialty apparel — 62% of borrowers above 4.0x leverage
 2. Non-food discount retail
 3. Retail REIT lending ...

Concentration headroom after shock: 4.1% (limit 12%, currently 9.6%)

reviews.name: Thomas Bradley
reviews.comment: The drawn versus contractual split is not optional in these papers and this prompt enforces it. Committee accepted the output with no rework.

reviews.name: Yvonne Hadley
reviews.comment: Runs in minutes against what used to be a multi-day slice. I still validate the migration matrix by hand for the top two bands.

prompts.title: Regulatory gap detector
prompts.description: Compares a new regulatory framework against internal policy and outputs the specific operational gaps to close.
prompts.repetition: Compresses a 500-page read into a working session
prompts.narrative: A regulatory update becomes an actionable gap list on day one instead of week six.
prompts.risk_note: Internal policy documents are confidential. The prompt runs inside the MUFG boundary and output is restricted to the Regulatory Change workspace.

tutorial.title: Reading a 500-page framework in an afternoon

guidelines: Use the controlled copy of the internal policy. A working draft will produce gaps that do not exist.
The gap list is an input to the Regulatory Change forum, not a compliance sign-off.
Where the rule text is ambiguous, the prompt must say so rather than resolve it — escalate to Regulatory Affairs.
Cite the paragraph number for every gap so the forum can verify it directly.
prompts.body:
ROLE: You are a regulatory risk analyst at MUFG.

INPUT: {{REGULATORY FRAMEWORK}} and {{INTERNAL POLICY}}
SCOPE: {{SCOPE}}

TASK
Ingest the attached update from the Basel Committee on Banking Supervision.
Compare its revised operational risk capital calculation rules against our
internal bank policy document attached. Output a bulleted list of all
specific operational gaps we must address.

FOR EACH GAP RETURN
- Rule paragraph reference and a one-line summary of the requirement
- The internal policy clause it maps to, or NO EQUIVALENT
- Gap type: process / data / system / governance / documentation
- Materiality: high / medium / low, with the reason
- Owning function and an indicative remediation window
- Whether the rule text is ambiguous (AMBIGUOUS — ESCALATE)

CONSTRAINTS
- Never paraphrase a rule without giving its paragraph number.
- Do not propose an interpretation where the text is unclear.
- Order the output by materiality, then by implementation deadline.
prompts.sample_output:
GAP ANALYSIS — 23 gaps (6 high, 11 medium, 6 low)

HIGH
1. §31.4 — Business indicator component must include leases
   Internal: Policy OR-04 §7 — NO EQUIVALENT
   Type: data | Owner: Finance Data | Window: 2 quarters
   Reason: understates BI by an estimated 3–5%

2. §33.9 — 10-year loss data history required
   Internal: OR-11 §2 holds 7 years
   AMBIGUOUS — ESCALATE: transition treatment for acquired entities ...

reviews.name: Laura Whitman
reviews.comment: The AMBIGUOUS flag is the feature. It refuses to invent an interpretation, which is exactly what you want when the regulator has not been clear.

reviews.name: Stephanie Lambert
reviews.comment: We now run this on every consultation paper the day it drops. Paragraph citations make the forum review fast.

reviews.name: David Carver
reviews.comment: Very good. On a 500-page input, split by chapter — one pass over the whole document is less precise on the low-materiality items.

prompts.title: AML and trade fraud pattern definer
prompts.description: Extracts behavioural anomalies from trade finance fraud case studies and drafts screening rules for the monitoring system.
prompts.repetition: Turns case study reading into ready-to-test rules
prompts.narrative: New typologies reach the screening engine in days rather than at the next policy cycle.
prompts.risk_note: Output feeds a control system. Every rule must be tested against historical data and approved by Financial Crime Compliance before deployment.
guidelines: Never deploy a generated rule directly. Backtest against 12 months of historical transactions first.
Estimate the false positive impact for every rule — the operations team owns the alert queue.
Financial Crime Compliance approval is mandatory before any rule reaches production.
Do not include live transaction data or customer names in the input.
prompts.body:
ROLE: You are a financial crime risk analyst at MUFG.

INPUT: {{FRAUD CASE STUDIES}}
Optional: {{CURRENT RULE SET}}
TARGET: {{TARGET SYSTEM}}

TASK
Review the recent trade finance fraud case studies provided by SWIFT.
Extract the key behavioural and structural anomalies — for example rapid
routing changes, shell company involvement, duplicate bill of lading —
and draft an instructional prompt for our transactional screening
algorithms to monitor.

FOR EACH TYPOLOGY RETURN
- Typology name and the case it derives from
- Observable data signals available in our systems
- Draft rule logic in plain language, then in pseudocode
- Expected false positive impact: high / medium / low, with reasoning
- Overlap with any existing rule in the current rule set
- Backtesting instruction: window, population, success criteria

CONSTRAINTS
- Only propose signals we can actually observe in MUFG data.
- Never include live transaction data or customer names.
- Flag any rule that could disproportionately affect a jurisdiction
  or client segment as REVIEW FOR BIAS.
prompts.sample_output:
TYPOLOGY 1 — Rapid routing change before shipment
Signals: SWIFT MT700 amendment count >2 within 5 days; consignee
country change post-issuance; new intermediary bank with <6mo history

Rule (plain): flag LCs amended more than twice in five days where the
amendment changes consignee country or adds an intermediary.
FP impact: MEDIUM — commodity trades amend legitimately at quarter end
Overlap: partial with TF-114, tighten rather than duplicate
Backtest: 12 months, all LC issuance, target <4% alert rate

TYPOLOGY 2 — Shell counterparty ... REVIEW FOR BIAS

reviews.name: Isaac Kendrick
reviews.comment: The bias review flag is a genuinely thoughtful inclusion. We have rejected two otherwise sensible rules because of it.

reviews.name: Hannah York
reviews.comment: The false positive estimate is directionally right but optimistic. Assume one band worse than it tells you.

prompts.title: VaR exception commentary generator
prompts.description: Explains a Value at Risk backtesting exception with the market drivers behind it, in the format the trading risk report expects.
prompts.repetition: Standardises daily commentary across six trading desks
prompts.narrative: Exception commentary is consistent across desks and ready before the morning risk call.
prompts.risk_note: Uses desk-level P&L and market data already published in the daily risk pack.

tutorial.title: Writing exception commentary that holds up

inputs.label: Market data summary
inputs.note: Rate, FX and credit moves for the day

guidelines: Attribution is a hypothesis. The desk head must confirm the driver before the commentary is published.
Do not restate the VaR number without the confidence level and holding period.
A clean exception is still an exception — never soften the language to avoid a regulatory count.
prompts.body:
ROLE: You are a market risk analyst at MUFG.

INPUT: {{VAR BACKTEST OUTPUT}}, {{MARKET DATA SUMMARY}}
DESK: {{DESK}}

TASK
Explain the VaR backtesting exception observed. Attribute the P&L move
to market drivers and write the commentary for the daily risk report.

RETURN
1. Exception summary: date, P&L, VaR at 99% 1-day, size of the breach
2. Attribution by risk factor, ranked by contribution
3. Whether the move was captured in the historical simulation window
4. Whether this is a model issue, a market event, or a position change
5. Rolling 250-day exception count and the regulatory traffic light status
6. 120-word commentary in the standard report register

CONSTRAINTS
- Always state the confidence level and holding period with any VaR figure.
- Do not soften the language. An exception is an exception.
- Mark attribution as hypothesis until confirmed by the desk head.
prompts.sample_output:
EXCEPTION — 6 Aug 2026, APAC rates trading
P&L −USD 18.4m vs VaR USD 14.1m (99%, 1-day) — breach of USD 4.3m

Attribution (hypothesis, pending desk head confirmation)
 1. JGB 10y +14bp intraday, steepener position   −USD 12.1m
 2. Basis widening, cross-currency book          −USD 4.8m
 3. Residual                                     −USD 1.5m

Historical window: move sits outside the 250-day window (largest prior 9bp)
Classification: market event, not model failure
Rolling exception count: 3 of 250 — GREEN

reviews.name: Laura Whitman
reviews.comment: Useful and consistent. It is a drafting aid, not an attribution engine — the desk head correction rate is still around one in three.

prompts.title: Sector deep-dive brief
prompts.description: Turns MUFG research and public filings into a two-page sector brief you can walk into a client meeting holding.
prompts.repetition: Replaces a half-day research trawl
prompts.narrative: You walk in knowing the sector as well as the client does.
prompts.risk_note: Operates on documents already held inside the MUFG boundary. No external transmission.

tutorial.title: Building a sector brief that lands

inputs.label: Meeting objective
inputs.note: What you want out of the meeting

guidelines: Use MUFG Research rather than third-party notes — licensing restricts what can be shared with clients.
The brief is internal preparation. Anything shared with the client needs Marketing sign-off.
Check the publication date; sector views older than a quarter should be refreshed with Research.
prompts.body:
ROLE: You are a corporate coverage banker at MUFG.

INPUT: {{SECTOR RESEARCH}}, {{CLIENT FILINGS}}
OBJECTIVE: {{MEETING OBJECTIVE}}

TASK
Produce a two-page sector brief covering:
1. Three forces reshaping the sector in the next 12 months
2. Where this client sits against peers on growth and leverage
3. The financing implication of each force
4. Five questions that will make the client think

CONSTRAINTS
- Every claim carries its source and date.
- No house view on the client's strategy — questions, not advice.
prompts.sample_output:
SECTOR BRIEF — Telecom infrastructure, APAC

FORCE 1  Fibre-to-tower consolidation (MUFG Research, 12 Apr 26)
  Client position: 34% of towers owned vs peer median 61%
  Financing implication: sale-and-leaseback releases est. USD 400m

FORCE 2  Spectrum renewal cycle concentrated in FY27 ...

reviews.name: Henry Tucker
reviews.comment: The five questions at the end are what make this worth running. Clients notice when you ask something their last banker did not.

prompts.title: Client profitability review
prompts.description: Reads the revenue and cost lines on an account and shows where the relationship makes or loses money.
prompts.repetition: Replaces a manual pull across four reporting systems
prompts.narrative: Shows which relationships are quietly unprofitable before the annual review does.
prompts.risk_note: Handles client or portfolio data. Mask identifiers before upload — the prompt stops if it detects an unmasked account number.
guidelines: Capital figures must come from the sanctioned RAROC report, not a desk estimate.
A loss-making product line is not a loss-making relationship — read the whole account before acting.
Do not share client-level profitability outside the coverage and credit teams.
prompts.body:
ROLE: You are a coverage banker reviewing relationship returns at MUFG.

INPUT: {{REVENUE REPORT}}, {{CAPITAL CONSUMPTION}}
PERIOD: {{REVIEW PERIOD}}

TASK
1. Revenue by product line, with year-on-year movement
2. Capital consumed and RAROC by facility
3. Products below the hurdle rate, ranked by capital drag
4. Three actions that would lift return without losing the relationship

CONSTRAINTS
- State the hurdle rate and the capital basis used.
- Separate committed from drawn exposure.
- Flag any product where revenue data is incomplete as PARTIAL.
prompts.sample_output:
RELATIONSHIP RETURN — FY26 YTD

Revenue        USD 14.2m (+8% YoY)
RAROC          9.1% vs 12% hurdle — below
Capital drag   Revolver (undrawn) consumes 46% of capital, 11% of revenue

ACTIONS
1. Reprice the undrawn commitment fee at renewal (+130bps RAROC)
2. Move FX flow onto our platform — PARTIAL data, confirm with Markets ...

reviews.name: James Whitfield
reviews.comment: Good discipline. It will not tell you to exit a client, which is right — it gives you the numbers and leaves the judgement alone.

prompts.title: Annual review pack summariser
prompts.description: Compresses a full annual review pack into the five things the credit committee will actually ask about.
prompts.repetition: Cuts a 60-page pack to a one-page read
prompts.narrative: You arrive at committee knowing which five slides will be challenged.
prompts.risk_note: Operates on documents already held inside the MUFG boundary. No external transmission.
guidelines: Check the summary against the pack before committee — a compressed number is still your number.
Any condition carried from last cycle must be addressed explicitly, not summarised away.
prompts.body:
ROLE: You are preparing a coverage banker for credit committee at MUFG.

INPUT: {{ANNUAL REVIEW PACK}}, {{PRIOR MINUTES}}

TASK
Identify the five points most likely to be challenged, and for each:
- The concern in one sentence
- The number or fact that triggers it
- The strongest answer available from the pack
- What is still missing

Then list any condition from the prior cycle not yet addressed.

CONSTRAINTS
- Rank by likelihood of challenge, not by page order.
- Mark UNANSWERED where the pack has no supporting evidence.
prompts.sample_output:
FIVE LIKELY CHALLENGES

1. Leverage rose to 3.4x against a 3.0x internal guide
   Answer available: 0.3x is the lease reclassification, not new debt
   Still missing: covenant headroom under the new definition — UNANSWERED

2. Two consecutive quarters of negative free cash flow ...

CARRIED CONDITION (not addressed): quarterly management accounts

reviews.name: Grace Alden
reviews.comment: The carried-conditions check has saved me twice. That is the question that catches people out.

prompts.title: Competitor displacement analysis
prompts.description: Works out which bank holds which product with a client, and where MUFG has a credible route in.
prompts.repetition: Replaces a manual read of public league tables
prompts.narrative: Turns "we are not lead bank" into a specific, winnable product target.
prompts.risk_note: Operates on documents already held inside the MUFG boundary. No external transmission.

tutorial.title: Finding the way into a locked relationship

guidelines: Public sources only. Never use information learned in a confidential context to build a competitive view.
Displacement takes cycles, not calls — treat the output as a 12-month plan.
prompts.body:

TASK

WALLET MAP — 7 products, 4 incumbents identified

Revolver        Bank A (lead)     renewal Sep 2027
Trade finance   no clear incumbent  ← ENTRY POINT 1
Cash management Bank B            regional only, APAC gap ← ENTRY POINT 2
FX hedging      Bank A            ...

reviews.name: Travis Fletcher
reviews.comment: Useful framing. The "no clear incumbent" line is where the wins actually are.

prompts.title: Syndication invitation memo
prompts.description: Drafts the invitation memo that goes to prospective syndicate members, from the approved term sheet.
prompts.repetition: Replaces a manual redraft for every syndication
prompts.narrative: Invitations reach the market the day the terms clear, not three days later.
prompts.risk_note: Deal-sensitive or control-facing. Restricted to a cleared team; every run is logged and reviewable by Compliance.

tutorial.title: Getting an invitation memo out fast

guidelines: Only credit-approved terms may appear. A draft term sheet in a market memo is a serious control breach.
Distribution requires a signed NDA from each recipient — the memo does not replace that check.
Legal reviews the memo before it leaves the building, every time.
prompts.body:
ROLE: You are a loan syndications associate at MUFG.

INPUT: {{APPROVED TERM SHEET}}, {{BORROWER OVERVIEW}}
TARGET: {{TARGET SYNDICATE}}

TASK
Draft the syndicate invitation memo covering transaction overview,

CONSTRAINTS

INVITATION — USD 500m Senior Unsecured Term Loan

TRANSACTION OVERVIEW
Borrower, facility, tenor and purpose as approved 8 Aug 2026.

KEY TERMS (as approved)
Margin, fees and covenants reproduced verbatim from the term sheet.
Ticket sizes: TO BE CONFIRMED with the bookrunner group ...

reviews.name: Rebecca Stone
reviews.comment: The refusal to round a number is the whole point. Market memos live and die on precision.

prompts.title: Equity story sense-check
prompts.description: Stress-tests a client equity story against the questions institutional investors are actually asking.
prompts.repetition: Replaces an informal round of desk feedback
prompts.narrative: Weak points surface in-house before they surface on a roadshow.
prompts.risk_note: Deal-sensitive or control-facing. Restricted to a cleared team; every run is logged and reviewable by Compliance.
guidelines: Deal-team only. An equity story in draft is highly price-sensitive.
The output is internal challenge, not investor guidance.
ECM confirms every valuation reference before it goes to the client.
prompts.body:
ROLE: You are an ECM analyst at MUFG challenging a draft equity story.

INPUT: {{DRAFT EQUITY STORY}}, {{PEER COMPARABLES}}

TASK
1. The three claims an institutional investor will test hardest
2. The evidence in the deck supporting each, and its weakest link
3. Where the story relies on a market forecast rather than a company fact
4. Five questions to expect on the first roadshow day

CONSTRAINTS
- Do not propose a valuation or a price range.
- Separate company-controlled outcomes from market-dependent ones.

HARDEST CLAIMS

1. "Margin expansion of 400bps by FY29"
   Evidence: cost programme with 60% already actioned
   Weakest link: remaining 40% depends on a systems migration with no date

2. "Addressable market growing 18% CAGR" — MARKET FORECAST, not company fact ...

reviews.name: Christopher Wade
reviews.comment: Good challenge tool. It is deliberately blunt, which is what a draft story needs.

prompts.title: M&A target long-list screener

prompts.risk_note: Handles client or portfolio data. Mask identifiers before upload — the prompt stops if it detects an unmasked account number.

guidelines: A long-list is a hypothesis. Nothing goes to the client before Sector and M&A review it.
Never include a company MUFG advises on the sell side without checking the conflicts list.
Where ownership is unclear, mark it rather than guessing.

INPUT: {{STRATEGY STATEMENT}}, {{SECTOR DATABASE}}
CRITERIA: {{SCREENING CRITERIA}}

TASK
Build a long-list of acquisition candidates, and for each return:
| Company | Sub-sector | Revenue | Ownership | Strategic fit | Likely availability |

Rank by strategic fit, then by likely availability.

CONSTRAINTS
- State the source and date for every financial figure.
- Mark ownership UNCLEAR rather than inferring it.
- Exclude anything on the conflicts list and say that you have.

LONG-LIST — 14 candidates, 5 high fit

1. Company A | Fibre infrastructure | EUR 210m rev | PE-owned, 2019 vintage
   Fit: closes the client's fibre gap | Availability: high, hold period matured

2. Company B | Tower services | UNCLEAR ownership — registry incomplete ...

prompts.description: Reads a client supplier list and payment terms to size a supply chain finance programme.

prompts.narrative: Sizes a programme in an afternoon that used to need a product workshop.

guidelines: Mask supplier identities before upload; tier and geography are enough for sizing.
Programme economics need Product sign-off — the output is an opportunity size, not a quote.
Check local regulatory treatment before proposing a cross-border programme.

ROLE: You are a transaction banking product advisor at MUFG.

INPUT: {{SUPPLIER PAYABLES}}, {{PAYMENT TERMS}}
GEOGRAPHIES: {{TARGET GEOGRAPHIES}}

TASK
1. Segment suppliers by spend concentration and current terms
2. Identify the tier where SCF creates the most mutual benefit

Likely uptake        35–55% of eligible spend in year one
WC released          USD 240–380m to the client

COMPLICATIONS: India (documentation), Indonesia (FX conversion rules)

reviews.name: Leah Harper
reviews.comment: Ranges rather than point estimates is the honest way to size these. Clients trust it more.

prompts.description: Spots client payment flows routed away from MUFG and quantifies what returning them is worth.
prompts.repetition: Replaces a manual flow reconciliation
prompts.narrative: Finds fee income already inside the relationship, just banked elsewhere.
prompts.risk_note: Handles client or portfolio data. Mask identifiers before upload — the prompt stops if it detects an unmasked account number.
guidelines: Flow data is confidential to the client relationship — never use it in a competitive pitch to another client.
Some flows are routed away for regulatory reasons. Check before treating one as leakage.

INPUT: {{PAYMENT ACTIVITY}}, {{ACCOUNT STRUCTURE}}

TASK
1. Map flows by corridor and identify which sit outside MUFG
2. Separate structural routing (regulatory, local requirement) from discretionary
3. Quantify annual fee value of the discretionary flows
4. Draft three talking points for the treasury conversation

CONSTRAINTS
- Label every corridor STRUCTURAL or DISCRETIONARY with the reason.
- Do not quote fee rates that are not in the published schedule.

FLOW REVIEW — 11 corridors

SGD→JPY   USD 340m/yr   DISCRETIONARY — no local requirement
IDR→USD   USD 90m/yr    STRUCTURAL — local settlement mandate
EUR→GBP   USD 210m/yr   DISCRETIONARY — legacy routing, no stated reason

reviews.comment: The structural versus discretionary split stops you walking into a meeting asking for something the client legally cannot move.

inputs.label: Trade activity summary
inputs.note: Volumes by corridor and counterparty type

Build a fit matrix: trade flow type × instrument in use × recommended instrument.
For each mismatch, state the cost or risk of the current arrangement.

- Note where the underlying commercial contract may mandate the instrument.

  Cost of current setup: est. USD 180k/yr in unnecessary LC fees
  CAUTION: check whether the sales contract mandates an LC

New counterparty, EM     | Open account | Confirmed LC recommended ...

reviews.name: Hannah York
reviews.comment: The contract-mandate caution is important. Half the "unnecessary" LCs I see are contractually required.

prompts.title: FX hedging conversation starter

APPETITE: {{CLIENT RISK APPETITE}}

TASK
1. Net exposure by currency after existing hedges
2. The two exposures with the largest earnings sensitivity
3. Three plain-language questions to open the conversation

- No directional view on any currency.

NET EXPOSURE AFTER HEDGES

THB   USD 180m unhedged — largest earnings sensitivity
KRW   USD 95m unhedged, natural offset in costs partially reduces this
EUR   fully hedged to policy ratio

QUESTIONS TO OPEN WITH
1. "Your THB exposure has roughly doubled since the policy was set..."

reviews.name: Lawrence Anderson
reviews.comment: It refuses to give a view or a level, which keeps coverage on the right side of the line. Exactly right.

TASK
1. Fixed versus floating split, and weighted average maturity
2. Annual interest cost impact under the scenario
3. The refinancing date where the impact concentrates
4. Three talking points in CFO language, no jargon

CONSTRAINTS
- Arithmetic only. Never present a rate forecast as a MUFG view.
- State the day count and reference rate assumptions used.

RATE SENSITIVITY — +100bps over 12 months

Floating share    62% of USD 2.1bn
Interest impact   +USD 13.0m annualised (SOFR, actual/360)
Concentration     USD 900m revolver reprices Q1 2027

TALKING POINT 1: "Roughly two-thirds of your stack reprices..."

reviews.name: Rachel Donovan
reviews.comment: Short and usable. I run it the morning after a central bank meeting.

prompts.title: ESG-linked loan structuring brief
prompts.description: Proposes sustainability-linked KPIs and margin ratchet mechanics grounded in the client own disclosures.

prompts.narrative: KPIs that survive second-party opinion, drafted in one pass.

guidelines: KPIs must be material to the client business — a second-party opinion will reject cosmetic targets.

FACILITY: {{FACILITY STRUCTURE}}

Propose three sustainability performance targets and the ratchet logic.

PROPOSED KPIs

KPI 1  Scope 1+2 emissions intensity, tCO2e per USD m revenue
       Baseline 2024: 41.2 (published, assured) | Ambition: −35% by 2029
       Reviewer risk: sector median trajectory is −30%, so this is credible

KPI 2  Renewable electricity share — NOT AMBITIOUS, already at 78% ...

reviews.name: Peter Lawson
reviews.comment: The "reviewer might reject it" line is the useful part. It saves a round trip with the second-party opinion provider.

prompts.title: Call note to CRM summary
prompts.description: Turns rough meeting notes into a structured CRM entry with follow-up actions and owners.
prompts.repetition: Removes 20 minutes of admin after every client meeting
prompts.narrative: Call notes actually get written, so the next banker inherits the relationship intact.
prompts.risk_note: Handles client or portfolio data. Mask identifiers before upload — the prompt stops if it detects an unmasked account number.

tutorial.title: Never write a call note from scratch again

inputs.label: Meeting notes
inputs.note: Rough notes, bullet form is fine

guidelines: Remove anything shared in confidence that the client would not expect to be recorded.
Material non-public information does not belong in the CRM — escalate it instead.
Confirm the actions and owners before saving; the model will infer an owner if you do not name one.
prompts.body:
ROLE: You are writing a client call note for the MUFG CRM.

INPUT: {{MEETING NOTES}}
ATTENDEES: {{ATTENDEES}}

TASK
Produce a structured call note:
- Purpose and outcome, two sentences
- Client priorities mentioned, with a direct quote where available
- Opportunities identified, mapped to a MUFG product
- Actions: what, who, by when
- Anything requiring escalation

- Never record information shared in confidence.

- If an action has no named owner, mark OWNER UNASSIGNED rather than guessing.

OUTCOME  Agreed to revisit the revolver ahead of the FY27 capex cycle.

OPPORTUNITIES  Cash pooling (Transaction Banking); revolver repricing.
